text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zimbabwe government has launched investigations into past business activities of former Lonrho Plc chief executive Tiny Rowland, who is alleged to have siphoned millions of dollars out of the southern African country using a shadow company known as Shepton in a possible massive tax evasion bid.

- Confusion reigned in the Zimbabwe capital Harare this week as to who had clinched the contract to build the Tokwe-Mukosi dam in Masvingo province, with an Italian firm claiming to have won it after talks with President Robert Mugabe in Rome although two local companies signed an accord with the government to build the same dam.
- The government was this week pressing authorities at the American computer company IBM Zimbabwe to immediately localise part of its equity in compliance with national investment laws.
- The Zimbabwe government has opened up road construction and maintanance to the private sector in continued efforts to involve private companies in the country's infrastructural development.

- Regional conglomerate Trans Zambezi Industries is seeking a listing on the Zimbabwe stock exchange in a move that will result in the localisation of Z$1.6 billion currently tied up in offshore investments.
- Four southern African countries including Zimbabwe have started a joint effort to root out rampant cross-border car racketeering which has cost them millions of dollars in insurance claims.
- Zimbabwean engineering firm Selmark, which won the takeover bid of troubled W.S. Craster last year, may lose the right to operate the company if it fails to raise Z$67 million within seven days.
- The Zimbabwe Council for Tourism said on Wednesday four areas of concern in the industry needed to be addressed urgently as they had a potential of derailing the booming sector.
